name: Primary Peritoneal Carcinoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Gynecologic Oncology Group (GOG) Criteria for Primary Peritoneal Carcinoma

criteria.description: Ovaries are either normal in size or enlarged due to benign processes, with minimal or no tumor involvement
Extensive involvement of the peritoneum by serous carcinoma with histologic features similar to ovarian serous carcinoma
Greater tumor involvement of extraovarian peritoneum compared to the surface of either ovary
Histopathologic confirmation of serous carcinoma consistent with primary peritoneal origin
No evidence of primary carcinoma elsewhere in the body

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria must be met including minimal ovarian involvement, predominant peritoneal disease, and histopathologic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of primary ovarian or other intra-abdominal carcinomas

imaging: CT scan showing diffuse peritoneal thickening and ascites
Ultrasound showing minimal or no ovarian masses
other: Histopathology revealing serous carcinoma with papillary structures
Immunohistochemistry positive for WT1 and PAX8

distinguishingFeatures: Greater ovarian tumor burden compared to peritoneum

redFlags: Rapidly increasing abdominal girth with ascites
Persistent pelvic or abdominal pain with no clear etiology
references: Prat J. Ovarian carcinomas: five distinct diseases with different origins, genetic alterations, and clinicopathological features. Virchows Arch. 2012.
Gynecologic Oncology Group. Primary peritoneal carcinoma diagnostic criteria. GOG Protocols.
Kurman RJ, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of Female Reproductive Organs. 4th Edition. IARC, 2014.
